land.text: east Ulaid, 'captured and held' at Downpatrick by John de Courcy in 1177

successors.note: Cliopatria's Earldom of Ulster (1326-1332) and the earldom-of-ulster dossier continue the land from 1205.

land.text: Inishowen from c. 465, Tyrone, Derry and Limavady from about 700

capitals.name: Emain Macha (Navan Fort)
capitals.note: 'its capital at Emain Macha'; the page gives two traditions for its fall (c. 331 and 450).

capitals.name: Downpatrick (Dun De Lethglaise)
capitals.note: The Dal Fiatach were 'based at Dun De Lethglaise (present-day Downpatrick)'; the page gives no years.

correction.text: 'the ancient territory of Ulaid spanned the whole of the modern province of Ulster, excluding County Cavan'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Ulaid. The extent is the page's legendary one; the infobox says 'Established: Before 450'. No area.

correction.text: Ulaid after the fall of Emain Macha (near Armagh) to the Three Collas: Ulster without Cavan and without the Airgialla lands (Armagh, Monaghan, Fermanagh)

keyframe_review.note: [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Armagh, Monaghan and Fermanagh are airgialla's 450 found region (Armagh only before the fix: Monaghan and Fermanagh, 14 H3 cells, were double-filled 450-699). Louth, also in airgialla's found region, is not drawn here (outside the Ulster region). New keyframe: the fall is dated 'around 331' by legend and 450 by 'Another tradition that survived until the 11th century'. Only Emain Macha's loss is placed; the Cruthin defeat at Moin Dairi Lothair (563) and the Airgialla settlement of Eilne are not mapped.

correction.text: Ulaid without the Airgialla lands and without Inishowen, where the Cenel nEogain are based from c. 465 (tir-eoghain); Tyrone and Derry stay Ulaid land until the 8th century

keyframe_review.note: [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Inishowen goes to tir-eoghain from 465 (Tir Eoghain page: 'The territory of Eoghan mac Neill was initially based in Inishowen'); the Ulaid page puts the Ulaid west of the Bann until the 8th century ('By the 8th century the territory of the Ulaid shrunk to east of the Bann'), so Tyrone, Derry and Limavady stay here until 700 and tir-eoghain gains them then (23 H3 cells were double-filled 465-699 before the fix). The rest of the land west of the Bann (Donegal beyond Inishowen, the Coleraine area) is drawn by nobody after 700: Cenel Conaill (Tir Chonaill) has no dossier.

correction.text: 'By the 8th century the territory of the Ulaid shrunk to east of the Bann'; the Dal Fiatach kingdom of Down and Antrim

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: council areas of Antrim and Down are the researcher's reading of 'east of the Bann'. 700 is a rounding of 'By the 8th century'.

region.text: the whole of Ulster without Cavan

ledger.note: Ulaid before 450: infobox 'Established: Before 450'; 'The Dal Fiatach dynasty held sway over Ulaid until the battle of Leth Cam in 827.' 400 is a bridge (confidence 1).

region.text: Armagh, Monaghan and Fermanagh, the Airgialla lands (Emain Macha, near Armagh, fell to the Three Collas)

ledger.note: 450: the fall of Emain Macha. 'Another tradition that survived until the 11th century dated the fall of Emain Macha to 450 AD'; legend says 'around 331 AD the Three Collas invaded Ulaid, destroyed its ancient capital Emain Macha'. The Airgialla are the page's successor state; the region is the researcher's reading. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] The region now equals airgialla's 450 found region without Louth (Armagh, Monaghan, Fermanagh); before the fix only Armagh was lost here.

region.text: Inishowen, the homeland of Eoghan mac Neill's Cenel nEogain

ledger.note: c. 465: the Cenel nEogain take Inishowen. The Tir Eoghain page (read for tir-eoghain) says 'The territory of Eoghan mac Neill was initially based in Inishowen' and its infobox gives 'c. 465: Eogan mac Neill (first)'; the Ulaid page puts all of Ulster except Cavan in the legendary Ulaid and says the Ulaid 'lost land to the Airgialla and the Northern Ui Neill', without naming Inishowen. Mirrors tir-eoghain's founding; a bridge, confidence 1.

region.text: Dal Riata in Scotland, settled by 'the Ulaid sub-group Dal Riata'

ledger.note: About 500: the Dal Riata settle in Scotland under Ulaid overlordship. 'Towards the end of the 5th century, the Ulaid sub-group Dal Riata' began settling in Scotland; the overlordship ended in 575. The start year is a bridge.

region.text: Dal Riata, freed from overlordship at Druim Ceit

ledger.note: 575: Dal Riata is freed from Ulaid's overlordship. 'The result of this pact was the removal of Dal Riata from Ulaid's overlordship' (Druim Ceit).

region.text: Tyrone, Derry and Limavady, west of the Bann: the Cenel nEogain spread out from Inishowen

ledger.note: By the 8th century: 'the territory of the Ulaid shrunk to east of the Bann' (Ulaid page). The page names the Airgialla and the Northern Ui Neill as the takers without a split; the Cenel nEogain land (Tyrone, Derry, Limavady) is assigned to tir-eoghain, whose page says the territory 'expanded out from there under his descendants' without a year. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Replaces the single 700 loss to airgialla, which airgialla's dossier never mirrored (Armagh, Monaghan and Fermanagh went in 450). 700 is a rounding; a bridge, confidence 1.

region.text: the rest of the land west of the Bann (Donegal beyond Inishowen, the Coleraine area), taken by the Northern Ui Neill

ledger.note: By the 8th century, as above: the Ulaid page names only 'the Northern Ui Neill' as taker; Donegal beyond Inishowen was the land of the other great Northern Ui Neill branch, the Cenel Conaill, who have no dossier (listed as tir-chonaill). Confidence 1: the split between the two branches is the researcher's reading.

region.text: east Ulaid, whose Dal Fiatach capital Dun De Lethglaise John de Courcy 'captured and held'

ledger.note: 1177: John de Courcy conquers Ulaid. 'In February 1177, John de Courcy left Dublin with a force of about 22 knights and 500 soldiers' and 'captured the town of Downpatrick'; the Ulaid page: 'Ulaid ceased to exist after its conquest in the late 12th century by the Anglo-Norman knight John de Courcy'; infobox 'Disestablished: 1177'. Ruaidri Mac Duinn Sleibe ruled 1172-1177. Month: February.
1177: Ulaid ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1177'; in 1205 de Lacy 'was made the first Earl of Ulster, founding the Earldom of Ulster'.

wars.name: Battle of Moin Dairi Lothair
wars.outcome: The Northern Ui Neill and an alliance of Cruthin kings fought at Moneymore; the Cruthin 'suffered a devastating defeat' and the Airgialla were settled in Eilne.
wars.note: The page does not say which side held which land before the battle.

wars.name: Battle of Moira
wars.outcome: 'the disastrous Battle of Moira in 637, in modern-day County Down, which saw Congal slain.'
wars.note: A Dal Riata and Ulaid battle; no territorial result is given.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Ulaid
wars.outcome: John de Courcy takes Downpatrick in February 1177 and holds it.

certainty.note: The legendary extent, the 450 and 700 shrinkages and the Bann frontier are all approximate.

sources.title: Ulaid
sources.note: Identity, extent, Emain Macha, Dal Riata, east of the Bann, 1177.

notes: Slug note: other batches asked for 'ulaid' (eu-11-d) and 'kingdom-of-ulaid' (eu-11-i); the Wikipedia article is 'Ulaid', so the slug is ulaid and the counterparts in lordship-of-ireland (kingdom-of-ulaid) should be read as ulaid; the orchestrator can alias. The Airgialla (successor on the page) need a dossier. Dal Riata's start is under Ulaid overlordship; the Dal Riata dossier names Ulaid as its infobox predecessor. Eilne, Cruthin territory and the Dal nAraidi are not mapped. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] After the review: (1) the 450 loss is Armagh, Monaghan and Fermanagh (airgialla's found region; Louth is outside the Ulster region this dossier draws, although the Ulaid page's legendary extent also took in Louth); (2) Inishowen is lost to tir-eoghain in 465 and Tyrone, Derry and Limavady in 700, both confidence 1 and mirrored in tir-eoghain; (3) the old 700 loss to airgialla is replaced by the tir-eoghain gain and a remainder to the Northern Ui Neill (counterpart string 'Cenél Conaill (Tír Chonaill)', no dossier). Gap left: dal-riata (other group) records a 644 loss of north-east Antrim to this state with no gain here, and the 499-575 overlordship of Dal Riata has no mirror there (Ulaid page: Dal Riata 'based in the Glens of Antrim'; 575 'removal of Dal Riata from Ulaid's overlordship').
